text:
maria: Heads-up — ACME on-prem fleet started failing after they applied our suggested CUDA 12.2 + driver 535 rollout. Pods requesting GPUs get stuck, nodes show no GPUs available. suspect customer-side driver/kernel mismatch.
jordan: Can you paste the node dmesg + `nvidia-smi` output?
maria: Sure — copied from one affected host: 
```
# /usr/bin/nvidia-smi
NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver.
Driver/library version mismatch
# dmesg | tail -n 20
[  123.456] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[  123.457] nvidia: Unknown symbol nvidia_pci_register_driver
[  123.458] nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout
[  123.459] nvidia: version magic '6.2.0-100-generic SMP mod_unload ' should be '5.15.0-60-generic SMP preempt'
```
maria: They say they are on a vendor-patched kernel (edge-vendor-rt-6.2) and won't bump kernel.
alex: That error looks like a kernel ABI mismatch — the driver was built against a different kernel headers. Did the driver come from our package or from the customer's custom packaging?
maria: Customer used vendor-supplied driver package (535 prebuilt .run), not DKMS.
sre_lead: If modules were prebuilt for 5.15 and the host kernel is 6.2, symbols/layout disagree. We should call this a supported-matrix gap for Private: prebuilt driver + custom kernels can fail.
jordan: Can we offer a quick workaround? Options: 1) Rebuild driver on-host (DKMS) — needs kernel headers (customer may not want to install), 2) Roll back to driver 525 (prebuilt for their kernel?) — risky, 3) Ship a container-side software fallback (MIG-less / CPU fallback) — reduces performance.
maria: Customer rejects kernel headers install (security policy). They asked if we can provide a driver variant that is ABI-compatible without rebuild.
alex: Not realistically — driver modules must match kernel. We could provide a small shim/compat layer but that's a non-starter.
sre_lead: Two action items: (A) Confirm supported matrix in the private docs and flag this customer kernel as unsupported, (B) propose escalated service: we offer a staged on-site driver rebuild under their security watch for a fee.
ops-bot: Ticket #INC-2026 created: "ACME onprem GPU driver/kernel mismatch" assigned to eng-infra oncall.
maria: Customer is pushing — they say this outage affects 120 GPUs (4 racks) and is blocking nightly batch. Estimated lost throughput = ~80 TB tokens/day. Need an ETA.
jordan: Short-term: ask them to reboot into a known-good kernel if available, or enable CPU fallback queues in their scheduler. Medium-term: require DKMS builds or kernel header access for any prebuilt driver installs.
alex: Also document that we won't accept prebuilt drivers for private deployments unless the customer certifies kernel version and ABI match. Add a checklist for customer onboarding.
sre_lead: I'll draft a KB entry and an onboarding checklist item. @maria please add exact node IDs and the customer's stated policy so support can price the remediation.
maria: Added node list to ticket. Customer asked about us supporting 'binary compatible drivers' across minor kernel versions — short answer?
jordan: Short answer: impossible to guarantee. Long answer: some distros maintain ABI compatibility across minor kernels, but vendor/custom kernels rarely do. We need to be clear in the private contract.
maria: Understood. I'll escalate with commercial.
deploy-bot: Deploy of docs patch "private-driver-requirements.md" scheduled for 1818001800.
sre_lead: :eyes: good. We should also run a quick audit of dedicated racks to ensure no similar unattended upgrades. Alex, can you run a query for any nodes that auto-upgraded to kernels >=6.0 in the last 7 days?
alex: On it — will post results shortly. :thumbsup:
